name: Claude Code Projects Beta
hook: Anthropic's biggest Claude Code announcement of September: Projects Beta (Sep 17) lets you spawn parallel cloud Claude Code sessions from a single project conversation, each a full Opus-backed instance running on its own branch. Select Pro/Max users get access first; others join a waitlist. Covered by The Register, Techstrong.ai, MLQ.ai, Times of AI, and four more outlets — the most press coverage a Claude Code feature has received this month.

name: Claude Code v2.1.277–278 — AGENTS.md + Auto Mode Classifier
hook: v2.1.277 (Sep 18) adds native AGENTS.md support — Claude reads AGENTS.md when no CLAUDE.md is present, bringing compatibility with the OpenAI/Codex convention. Also ships: server-side auto mode classifier (eliminates overhead charges for API/Enterprise/Bedrock/Vertex users), VS Code agent map view, and background task status indicators. v2.1.278 (Sep 19) follows with ~55 fixes. These two releases triggered a cluster of new AGENTS.md tooling (see backpass, ossrules, abide, agent-rules-skill below).

name: ponytail
hook: 141K-star code-efficiency skill that reduces the amount of code Claude writes by 54% and token consumption by 22% — achieved by strict scope enforcement and a structured clarification gate. Still the dominant general-purpose efficiency skill in the ecosystem. First appeared Sep 7–11; consistently ranking in the top-3 most-installed skills week over week.

name: cloudflare/security-audit-skill
hook: 15.6K stars and still accelerating — Cloudflare's official security-audit skill gained +2.6K stars in just 48 hours (Sep 16–18), making it one of the fastest single-week growth events for a Claude Code skill. Runs 681 security checks across OWASP Top 10, cloud misconfigs, and secrets exposure; outputs structured SARIF reports you can feed directly into CI. Enterprise teams are adopting it as a mandatory pre-commit hook.
recurring_note: Recurring — 15.6K stars (up from 13K on Sep 16), +2.6K in 48 hours

name: abide
hook: 124 stars, Show HN this week. Abide enforces AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md rules per-edit via TypeSafe Jev checks — so policy violations are caught before a file is saved, not after a code review. Each check costs ~$0.00004, making continuous enforcement economical at scale. Perfectly timed with v2.1.277's AGENTS.md support: one tool to write the rules, another to enforce them.

name: backpass
hook: 1.1K stars. 'Gradient descent for your AGENTS.md' — backpass reads your session transcripts, identifies patterns in what worked and what didn't, and proposes evidence-backed diffs to your AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md. A human gate runs before any change is written. Released the same week v2.1.277 shipped AGENTS.md support; the timing has driven rapid adoption among teams iterating on agent behavior.

name: compact-adviser
hook: 118 stars. Classifies whether to run /compact using two Jev questions rather than always compacting at a fixed threshold — saving tokens when compaction isn't needed. The confidence threshold self-adjusts from 0.90 down to 0.50 as context fills, so it gets more aggressive about compacting right when it matters most. Works inside Claude Code hooks with no manual invocation.

name: typesafe-computer-use
hook: 429 stars. Replaces Claude Opus 5 for computer-use decisions with OCR + a TypeSafe Jev classifier: $0.0002/decision vs $0.032 for Opus 5, 155× cheaper, and 14–40× faster latency. Targets macOS Claude Code users who run computer-use tasks at scale — form filling, UI testing, scraping — and can't afford Opus 5's per-call cost in a high-frequency loop.

name: claudex-loop
hook: 2.2K stars, up from 1.7K since the Sep 9 digest — a 29% increase in 10 days. Chase AI's (109K subs) own Claude Code productivity loop: structured task decomposition, automatic context checkpointing, and a resumable session protocol. The growth rate is accelerating as the channel's audience converts to users.
recurring_note: Recurring — grew from 1.7K → 2.2K stars since Sep 9 (+29%)

name: advertising-ops (CMO in a Box)
hook: 86 stars. Scrapes long-running Meta Ad Library ads, tears down video creative frame-by-frame, then generates aligned copy and image/video variations — a full creative analysis and production pipeline inside Claude Code. Charlie Automates (8K subs) featured it as their 'Claude Code Jarvis AI that runs my business' in a Sep 15 video, driving a notable star spike for a small channel.

name: agent-rules-skill
hook: 76 stars. Auto-generates AGENTS.md files following the agents.md convention — supporting Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, and Cursor simultaneously. A natural companion to v2.1.277's new AGENTS.md support: run the skill once and get a properly structured file that all three agents can read. Reduces setup friction when a team wants consistent agent behavior across tools.

name: ossrules
hook: 25 stars. A curated library of real AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md files from production open-source projects, each with annotations explaining the rationale behind key rules. Public JSON API so tools like backpass and agent-rules-skill can pull from it as reference material. Landed the same week v2.1.277 shipped, filling the 'show me real examples' gap.

name: AAS Core — Agentic Awesome Skills
hook: 46.6K stars, updated Sep 19. The largest curated skills catalog in the ecosystem — 2,115+ agentic skills across dev, security, infra, product, and marketing — with a local MCP catalog, CLI, plugins, and Workbench. Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI, and 10+ other agents. Still growing; new skills added daily.
recurring_note: Recurring — 46.6K stars, updated Sep 19 with new skills

name: i-dont-believe-you
hook: 16 stars. A stop-hook skill that runs 8 shell verification commands before an agent can claim tests pass: checks for disabled tests, removed assertions, swallowed errors, skipped suites, and mocked-away dependencies. Closes the most common agent honesty gap — Claude (and other agents) sometimes declare success when tests were quietly neutered. Small but solves a real trust problem.

name: explain-diff-html
hook: 7 stars, first appearance in any digest. Transforms PRs and raw diffs into self-contained interactive HTML walkthroughs: background context, design intuition, code flow in execution order, and an embedded quiz to verify reviewer comprehension. Each output is a single portable HTML file — no server required. Useful for async code reviews where reviewers lack context on the original intent.
